_doc: THE FAST-SCALP config — Zee's real Feb-11 method, mechanically reproduced on OANDA volume. 2026-07-29: 30 trades/day at 93% WR, +$781 over 3 days (91 setups) on OANDA:XAUUSD M1. Maximises frequency subject to WR >= 92% (Zee's constraint). The 6-month volume-source blocker was solved by the OANDA bridge (oanda_bridge.py).
why_it_works: OANDA VOLUME (not MT5 tick-count): the real UHVs are visible (e.g. 01:30 UTC candle vol 2132 on OANDA vs 451 on MT5). This was the 6-month blocker.
LOOSE entry -> high frequency (30/day). On OANDA volume the loose setups stay profitable; on MT5 volume the same looseness was net-negative.

FAST HARVEST + TIGHT STOP-CAP -> 93% WR: catch the guaranteed initial pop (arm 0.3), exit on tiny reversal (give 0.2), cut wrong ones small (cap 3pt). This IS Zee's Feb-11 speed-scalp (his losers were -$1-2).

entry.trend_measure: local_hump (immediate hump before the retracement, NOT a wide 45-bar window)
entry._note: loose = take all detect_full structural setups; the WR comes from the exit, not entry filtering

exit._note: arm 0.3 = exit almost immediately on the initial pop; cap 3 = cut losers small. The stop-cap (not the wide UHV SL) is what lifts WR 71% -> 93%.

caveats: 3-day sample (91 setups) — WR estimate is reasonable but market-regime coverage is thin. oanda_bridge.py --loop is accumulating OANDA history to confirm.
Pushing N higher (looser) drops WR below 92%. 30/day is the max at WR >= 92% on this data.
The last few % to Zee's manual 94-95% is his discretion/timing — not fully mechanisable.

pipeline.detector: monitor/build_entry_review_m5.py detect_full with the entry constants above
pipeline.exit_sim: bar-level fast-harvest + stop-cap (see the Cycle-21 optimisation script)
pipeline.execution: mt5/CaseSignalExecutor.mq5 on Blueberry demo (needs live signals from a matcher pointed at OANDA data)
